head: Verb
Main job
Example
rows: what someone or something is: identity, origin, profession, characteristics, time
Soy estudiante. Es de Sevilla. Son las tres.
where something is and how someone is right now
there is, there are: something exists
Hay un banco en la calle.
to have: possessions, age, feelings, obligations
Tengo un coche. Tengo 20 años. Tengo hambre.

blocks.title: Dutch has one verb, Spanish has two
blocks.text: Dutch zijn becomes ser or estar. Ask yourself: am I saying what it is (identity, characteristic) or where or how it is right now (location, temporary state)? The first is ser, the second estar.

head: Use ser for
Example
English
rows: Hoy es lunes. Son las dos.
Today is Monday. It is two o'clock.
Ella es mi madre. Es de Pedro.
She is my mother. It is Pedro's.

blocks.title: Memory trick: DOCTOR
blocks.text: The six uses spell DOCTOR: Description, Occupation, Characteristic, Time, Origin, Relationship. Jobs take no article after ser: Soy médico, not Soy un médico (unless you add an adjective: Soy un buen médico).

blocks.label: irregular · where and how something is

blocks.title: Memory trick: PLACE
blocks.text: PLACE: Position, Location, Action, Condition, Emotion. If you ask ¿Dónde está…? (where is…?) you always use estar: ¿Dónde está el baño? Está al fondo.
4. Ser or estar? The same adjective, a different meaning

head: ser: what it is like
estar: how it is right now
rows: Soy nervioso. (I am a nervous person.)

blocks.text: Hay means there is and there are. It never changes, for singular and plural alike (Dutch: er is / er zijn). It introduces something new or indefinite: un, una, unos, unas, a number, mucho, algún or no article at all.

head: Example
English
rows: Hay un museo en la ciudad.
There is a museum in the city.
Hay tres chicos en la puerta.
There are three boys at the door.
Is there a bank around here?

blocks.title: Hay or está?
blocks.text:
hay = a new or indefinite thing: Hay un banco en la calle Mayor.
estar = a known or definite thing (el, la, mi, este…): El banco está en la calle Mayor.
Never combine hay with el, la, mi or este: Hay el banco is wrong.

blocks.title: Age: Spanish says “have”, not “be”
blocks.text: Dutch says ik ben 20. Spanish says Tengo 20 años (literally: I have 20 years). Always include años. To ask: ¿Cuántos años tienes?
Tengo que estudiar esta noche. (I have to study tonight.)  ·  Tenemos ganas de viajar. (We feel like travelling.)

rows: Spanish gives age with tener, and always says años.
A profession is what someone is: ser.
Tiredness is a temporary state: estar.
Hunger, thirst, cold and heat use tener, not estar.
Hay el libro en la mesa.
Hay un libro en la mesa. / El libro está en la mesa.
Hay needs an indefinite noun. A definite noun takes estar.
Están dos libros en la mesa.
Hay dos libros en la mesa.
To say that something exists, use hay.

blocks.text: Complete each sentence with ser, estar, hay or tener in the right form. Answers are on the last page.

items.q: En mi ciudad ______ un museo grande.
items.full: En mi ciudad hay un museo grande.
Son las cinco de la tarde.

items.q: There are two books on the table.
items.a: Hay dos libros en la mesa.

items.q: The keys are in the kitchen.
items.a: Las llaves están en la cocina.
